fun_highlights: The four callings (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer) are genuinely structural — each gates its own 3-4 card arc that makes a soldier's late life read unmistakably different from a scholar's, and this is the game's strongest single lever for variety.

The callback system is the best mechanic in the game. When the outcast from the yard returns twenty years later as a benefactor, or the old love surfaces in a newspaper column, or the corner you cut comes back demanding a larger dishonesty, the reach-back is emotionally earned and creates the sensation of a life that coheres.

Era-plus-vocation intersections (vx_scholar_turning, vx_soldier_war, vx_maker_plenty) are rare but excellent — the scholar humbled by younger thinkers in a turning age, the soldier who faces the real war they trained for, land with specificity that the general cards lack.

The competing-goods cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) are the closest the game gets to truly agonising choices — both options carry genuine cost, and neither is coded as the 'right' answer.

The dynasty layer — motto, heirlooms, the seat climbing from 'nothing but a name' to 'a fine townhouse', repute drifting across generations — creates a genuine 'one more dynasty' pull and makes some lives feel like they carry history.
staleness: The love-and-marriage pipeline is deeply grooved by dynasty 4. In the 15-dynasty transcript, a_meet_late fires as the love entry point in the majority of adult lives, and a_marry is resolved with 'Ask. Build a life.' in roughly 18 of 20 eligible cases. The engine tries to spread love across ages but the transcripts still cluster. The player's choice at the marriage card almost never diverges.

The binary open/close grammar is unrelenting. Even the 'competing goods' cards present as two labelled options with legible polarity. A shrewd, cold character and a warm, open-handed one face the same set of frames ('tell the truth / spare them', 'keep the promise / release yourself') and the right answer is usually readable from the character they've built. Choices feel like confirmations of type rather than tests.

The adult band (26-45) is the stalest section. After vocation-specific cards land once, the shared pool dominates: a_work (promotion vs presence), a_child, a_affair, x_honest_or_kind, a_belief — these recur across nearly every life with a family and have identical framing regardless of who is living them. A scholar and a maker both face the same evening-or-title dilemma with the same text.

The callback payoffs are high-quality but there are fewer than the game's ambition requires. In the 15 dynasties, cb_books_late, cb_outcast_return, and cb_strayed/cb_unspoken are the callbacks that reliably land with weight; others (cb_trade_regret, cb_home_keep) are narrower and less often triggered. A life with no callback feels incomplete, and several in the transcripts have none at all.

Choices rarely produce surprising downstream consequences the player couldn't predict. The 'strayed' flag opens cb_strayed in old age, but the player knows this is coming. The 'chose_soldier' flag gates the soldier arc, but which soldier cards fire is invisible. There is no moment equivalent to 'I did not know that choice would matter this way' — the gates are legible from the outside.

The elder band goes stale fastest across a dynasty. By the 8th life, e_legacy (what do you want remembered), e_garden/e_last_walk/e_peace, and the body-slow observe lines are a near-certain sequence. The variation is prose-level (different epitaph lines, different legacy choices), not structural. Dying reads the same shape every time.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 choice options that are only unlockable by specific life histories — options the player cannot see unless they have a relevant memory. For example, on a_work, a third option 'Teach what you know — take your best apprentice with you' gated on became_teacher, or on a_marry a 'Make a contract, not a vow' option gated on chose_trade. These would make the player feel their choices built something invisible and specific.
improvements.why: The binary grammar makes choices feel like the game asking 'warm or cold?' A third option that only exists because of who you became turns choice into discovery and makes prior decisions feel genuinely generative rather than stat-adjusting.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 vocation-specific reframings of the shared adult cards. The a_work card should read differently for a soldier (the campaign versus the family), a scholar (the paid lectureship versus the question), a maker (the commission versus the personal work). Same stakes, same beat, but voiced through who this person actually is.
improvements.why: Right now the adult band is shared text regardless of calling. The vocation arc adds dedicated cards, but the 70% of adult life that is shared template ignores who the player chose to be at 18. Vocation-aware text would make the calling feel like it permeates the life, not just its dedicated cluster.

improvements.what: Introduce at least one choice per life whose downstream consequence is delayed and non-obvious — the player cannot predict which card it enables. For instance, refusing the affair ('Close the door') could, 15 years later, trigger a card where the temptation returns but in a different form entirely (a business partner, a rekindled old connection) — not flagged as 'this is about that'. The gap between cause and effect is what creates the feeling that the simulation is watching.
improvements.why: Currently every callback is legible: cb_strayed follows strayed, cb_books_late follows child_books. The player can trace the wire. True surprise — the kind that makes you sit back and say 'that came from the thing I did at 24' — would require non-obvious connections with a longer delay.

improvements.what: Diversify the love entry point. The a_meet_late card is currently the most common love opener in the transcripts despite engine efforts to spread it. Add 2-3 distinct love-entry cards for youth (besides y_love1): one for soldiers in barracks, one for scholars at study, one for wanderers on the road — each voiced in the register of that life. This would prevent the 'late love across a counter on an ordinary Tuesday' line from becoming the dynasty's ambient soundtrack.
improvements.why: When the same prose construction — 'later than the stories say it should be / someone' — lands in dynasty 3, 5, 7, and 9, the player stops reading it. Vocation-gated love cards would let the calling shape even this most personal beat.

improvements.what: Give the elder band a structural fork that depends on how the life was lived — not just which elder cards fire, but whether an elder gets an 'accounting' arc (a reckoning with the shape of a whole life, open to those with high spirit and many decisions made) or a 'drift' arc (a quieter close, available to those with low spirit or few choices). This would make dying feel different depending on whether the player engaged or receded throughout the life.
improvements.why: Currently every elder band resolves through the same pool regardless of what came before. The epitaph is the only differentiation at death, and epitaphs are elegant but short. A structurally divergent elder arc would make the whole game feel like it has been watching.

verdict: A Life has a genuinely moving callback system and real vocation-level structural variety, but the adult band's shared template and the binary grammar's legible polarity mean that by dynasty 6-8 the player is savouring the prose rather than the choices — which is not the same thing as meaningful, characterful decision-making.
